_note: Direction-of-travel map for the AI Engineering section. daily_facts.py picks one theme per day (date-seeded permutation); the model then chooses a specific topic within or adjacent to it and researches it with web search. Examples are examples, not limits. Editing this list mid-cycle reshuffles the rotation once.
summary: AI Engineering is the practice of building reliable production systems around LLMs: deciding what goes into the model's context, retrieving knowledge, letting models call tools and act in loops, coordinating agents, keeping memory and state, constraining outputs, evaluating and observing behaviour, adding guardrails and human oversight, routing between models for cost and quality, and running all of it through a disciplined development lifecycle. New practices and terms appear constantly.

themes.name: Context engineering
themes.description: Deciding what information enters the model's context window, in what form, and what is left out.

themes.name: Retrieval and RAG
themes.description: Grounding model answers in external knowledge retrieved at query time.

themes.name: Agentic loops and planning
themes.description: Letting a model act repeatedly: observe, decide, call tools, check results, and continue until done.

themes.name: Tool use and structured outputs
themes.description: Getting models to call functions and emit machine-readable outputs that software can trust.

themes.name: AI memory and agent state
themes.description: How agents remember across turns and sessions, and how their working state is stored and resumed.

themes.name: Multi-agent systems and orchestration
themes.description: Coordinating several models or agents, and the workflows that sequence them.

themes.name: Harness engineering
themes.description: Building the scaffolding around a model (tools, permissions, loops, environment, feedback) that turns it into a capable agent.

themes.name: Evaluation and evals
themes.description: Measuring whether an AI system actually does what it should, before and after changes.

themes.name: Observability and tracing
themes.description: Seeing what an AI system did in production: inputs, outputs, tool calls, latency and cost.

themes.name: Guardrails and safety
themes.description: Constraining what an AI system will accept and produce, and defending against misuse.

themes.name: Model routing and cost
themes.description: Choosing which model handles which request, trading quality against latency and cost.

themes.name: Human-in-the-loop systems
themes.description: Designing where and how people review, approve or correct AI behaviour.

themes.name: Agent development lifecycle and production architecture
themes.description: How AI systems are designed, tested, deployed and operated over time.

themes.name: Frameworks and patterns
themes.description: The libraries and design patterns practitioners use to build AI systems.

themes.name: Emerging practices
themes.description: Newly named techniques, terms or architectural ideas that AI engineers have started discussing recently. Prefer something from the last few months.
